lines.text: [Instrumental Intro — teasing fiddle begins a frantic chromatic bumblebee run; harmonica answers; banjo and dobro interrupt; escalating four-way chase; hard stop]
[Verse 1 — stomping acoustic groove, dry amused baritone]
She don’t ask—she announces
What the rest of us will do
Drops a royal little “You should”
Like the thought belonged to you
And if the kingdom doesn’t answer
On the first obedient ring
She can fill a room with winter
Without saying anything
[Pre-Chorus — instruments begin buzzing underneath]
I was raised beneath that weather
I could read it by degrees
Knew exactly when to surrender
To preserve Her Majesty’s peace
[Chorus — full band, swaggering]
Here comes the flight of the queen bee
Crown cutting into the wind
One little sigh and the old damn hive
Goes marching out again
But I don’t run on royal time now
I don’t kneel and I don’t flee
She can circle till the sun goes down—
Her kingdom ends where I begin
[Instrumental Chase — fiddle states the frantic classical figure; banjo challenges; harmonica mocks; dobro answers low; all four collide]
[Verse 2 — groove returns heavier]
She can make a favor sound like
Something you already owe
Turn “I need” into a summons
Then act wounded when you don’t
Every kindness has a memory
Every sacrifice, a frame
She’ll hang herself above the mantel
Then let you supply the nails
But I know that little pageant
I’ve played every part before
The villain, fool and rescue crew
All entering through one door
Now I leave the crown to glitter
And the curtain where it falls
I’ve got better things to carry
Than the weight of it all
[Chorus — harder, instrumental stings between lines]
Here comes the flight of the queen bee
Crown cutting into the wind
One little sigh and the old damn hive
Goes marching out again
But I don’t run on royal time now
I don’t kneel and I don’t flee
She can circle till the sun goes down—
Her kingdom ends where I begin
[Verse 3 — confident, no self-pity]
I’ll still lift what she can’t carry
Still show up when we agree
I can give without surrender
I can love and still be free
She may never call it asking
I may never hear her say
“I know your time belongs to you, son”—
Hell, we all need dreams someday
I spent years mistaking tension
For the price of being good
Thought a man proved that he loved you
By abandoning what he should
Now her sorrow is her weather
And my answer can be no
I don’t have to curse the thunder
I just don’t have to go
[Breakdown — nearly bare; boot stomp, dobro, close baritone]
Let the phone ring.
Let the sad face glow.
Let the silence put on sackcloth
For the tragedy of “no.”
No trial.
No defense.
No closing argument from me.
I’ve got work beneath my own two hands.
I’ve got somewhere else to be.
[Instrumental Build — banjo and dobro duel; fiddle and harmonica pile in; drums rise]
[Final Chorus — explosive but rootsy]
There goes the flight of the queen bee
Crown shaking in the wind
One little sigh—but this old worker
Ain’t marching out again
I don’t run on royal time now
I don’t kneel and I don’t flee
She can circle till the sun goes down—
Her kingdom ends where I begin
[Four-instrument swarm — furious fiddle, harmonica, banjo and dobro; sudden half-time stop]
I thought the flight belonged to her—
All that buzzing majesty
[Dead stop]
Turns out the one who found his wings
Was me
[Outro — warm, grounded; sparse acoustic and dobro]
I can love her.
Let her be.
And own the life that belongs to me.
[Final instrumental sting — one impossibly fast shared run; hard stop]
